0.2.2 is 0.2.1 with npm published through trusted publishing: npm verifies that each version was built by this repository's release workflow, and no npm token exists any more. The library is unchanged since 0.2.0. 0.2.1 published 0.2.0's code everywhere; its npm packages are scoped (`@shayxo.dev/liquidglass`, `@shayxo.dev/liquidglass-react-native`).

Liquid Glass for Compose Multiplatform, measured against iOS recordings. 0.2 replaces 0.1.0's API, adds glass versions of the Material 3 components, and brings the material to the web and .NET.

## Install

```kotlin
// build.gradle.kts: adds liquidglass, and liquidglass-material3 when the module uses Material 3
plugins { id("dev.shayxo.liquidglass") version "0.2.2" }
```

Then `./gradlew liquidGlassAdopt` switches an app's Material 3 imports to the glass versions once (`--dry-run` lists the changes first). Or use the BOM, `dev.shayxo.liquidglass:liquidglass-bom:0.2.2`, or plain artifacts. See [Getting started](https://liquidglass.shayxo.dev/getting-started/).

## New

- **One way in, named after SwiftUI's API.**
  - `LiquidGlassTheme { App() }` once at the root.
  - Then `Modifier.glassEffect(Glass.Regular.tint(c).interactive(), shape)` on anything, at any depth.
  - `GlassEffectContainer` merges nearby glass with a liquid neck.
  - `glassEffectID` morphs a piece that reappears.
  - Nothing has to be marked as a backdrop.
- **`liquidglass-material3`.** Glass versions of the Material 3 components, with the same names and parameters. Material's anatomy stays; iOS 26 shapes and motion are drawn in the app's colours.
  - Bars, buttons, chips, cards, dialogs, sheets with a partial stop, menus, tooltips, drawers, pickers, sliders, tabs and search.
  - Panels are frosted, and controls on a panel take its frost.
  - Back and Escape dismiss overlays.
- **Gradle plugin `dev.shayxo.liquidglass` and a BOM.**
- **Web.**
  - A `wasmJs` target with the same shaders as desktop.
  - On npm, `@shayxo.dev/liquidglass`: a `<liquid-glass>` custom element for any framework.
  - The element's HTML engine refracts the live page in Chromium and frosts it elsewhere; its canvas engine draws the production shaders.
- **React Native, on npm.** `@shayxo.dev/liquidglass-react-native` provides `GlassSurface` and `GlassLens` for a React Native Skia `<Canvas>`, on Android and React Native Web, drawn with the production shaders.
- **Flutter, from source.** `ports/flutter` provides `GlassSurface`, which refracts the live Flutter backdrop on Impeller with the material shader translated from the Compose library. It is not on pub.dev yet; depend on it by path. Checked on a Pixel 7 (Impeller on Vulkan) and the Android emulator (OpenGL ES).
- **.NET on NuGet.**
  - `LiquidGlass`: a SkiaSharp painter.
  - `LiquidGlass.WinForms`, `LiquidGlass.Wpf` and `LiquidGlass.Avalonia`: glass over each toolkit's native content.
- **Optics.**
  - iOS 27's measured rim, with its dark outer contour, is opt-in through `GlassStyle.outerContour` and `GlassTabBarStyle.Ios27`.
  - The tab bar's selector and motion are recalibrated against iOS 26 recordings.

## Breaking

0.1.0's `LiquidGlassScene`, `LiquidGlassState`, `Modifier.liquidGlassSource` and `Modifier.liquidGlass` are removed. Wrap the app in `LiquidGlassTheme` and use `Modifier.glassEffect`. `GlassTabBar` takes no state. The [API reference](https://liquidglass.shayxo.dev/api-reference/#removed-18-october) maps every removed name to its replacement.

## Limits

- Motion and material are close to the iOS recordings but not identical. The remaining differences are [listed](https://liquidglass.shayxo.dev/research/divergences/).
- Glass draws above other content, and an ancestor's alpha does not fade it.
- The web component's lensing is Chromium-only.

The full log is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/shayann07/liquidglass/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
